newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine may issue 18-m, 2-yr T-bills soon-c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine may issue 18-m, 2-yr T-bills soon-c.bank.

text.p: Ukraine may soon begin issuing Treasury bills with maturities of 18 months and two years to meet increased demand for longer-term bills, the head of the central bank said on Tuesday.
"We think that in the next month and a half it will be necessary for us to begin issuing 18-month and two-year T-bills," National Bank of Ukraine Chairman Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference.
Yushchenko said demand for nine- and 12-month paper had increased in the last six weeks.
The Finance Ministry, which issues the T-bills sold by the central bank, has been limiting volumes on securities in recent weeks to steer non-resident buyers towards buying longer-term bills.
Top bank and ministry officials have said they want to increase participation by Ukrainian banks, after estimating that non-residents were taking up to 80 percent of the market.
Yushchenko repeated promises made two weeks ago to issue new regulations soon limiting non-resident activity on the Treasury bill market, but did not go into details.
"We understand that the participation of non-residents as it is going on today is increasingly being viewed as negative," he said.
"The role of commercial banks has been going down and there has been an increase in what we call "clients" -- residents and non-residents," Yushchenko said.
Average yields have fallen to 27.1 percent in the last week of January from 49.4 percent in the first week due to lowered issue volumes, he added.

Foreign buyers, which include Western banks and banks from Latvia, Lithuania, Cyprus and the Czech Republic, have been attracted by high yields, a relatively stable hryvnia currency and slowed inflation.
